version.changelog:
Version 0.2.1

- Updated documentation for clarity and improved conciseness in README.md and SKILL.md.
- Removed redundant file: skill-card.md.
- No changes to code or functionality; documentation-only update.

llm.summary: This is a coherent inbound-lead skill, but it needs review because anonymous form submissions can update shared contact records and send unescaped personal data into Slack.

dimensions.detail: Use of LinkedIn enrichment, Slack posting, shared GTM models, and optional Anthropic/web-search research is purpose-aligned, but the public-to-internal data boundary is under-scoped: public form content is trusted for record mutation and rendered as Slack Markdown without escaping.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is disclosed as Cargo CDK cookbook copying plus a website SDK dependency, with deploy gated behind plan output and explicit user approval. No OS-level persistence, shell backdoor, or remote code retrieval behavior was found in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill is unusually explicit about setup, placeholders, privacy-page review, origin allowlisting, explicit deploy approval, and the research play shipping disabled. I found no prompt-hijacking or hidden reviewer instructions in the artifact text.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates durable Cargo resources, shared model columns, a public form, and a disabled scheduled research play. The persistence is disclosed and product-level rather than system-level, but users should review it because it affects ongoing inbound data flows.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the main behavior: a public demo form enriches work-email domains, qualifies leads, writes GTM account/contact records, posts Slack alerts, and optionally researches qualified leads. The concern is that unauthenticated submissions are upserted into shared contact records by email and can overwrite existing identity, account, qualification, metadata, and consent fields.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, change the workflow so unauthenticated form submissions cannot overwrite authoritative contact records unless the email is verified, or restrict updates to append-only submission fields. Escape or plain-text render all Slack fields, limit message lengths, validate page URLs, and confirm the privacy notice covers company enrichment, Slack sharing, model storage, retention, and the optional research play.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The referenced files flagged as partial are present in the workspace and were inspected, including evals/contract.mjs and the referenced infra files; I did not find evidence of analysis evasion from missing artifacts.
[P9] expected: The long spaces occur in Markdown table alignment in SKILL.md. Manual inspection found no hidden instructions or off-screen payload in those sections.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending submitted contact data to shared records and Slack is central to the skill and is disclosed. The skill also requires an operator-reviewed privacy section, but users still need to confirm disclosure, retention, and channel access controls before deployment.
[T05] unexpected: The public form intentionally upserts by submitted email, but allowing an unauthenticated visitor to update existing shared contact fields is broader than needed for inbound routing and remains the main Review concern.
[T09] unexpected: Posting to a fixed Slack channel is expected, but interpolating public form fields into Markdown without escaping is unnecessary and can let a submitter manipulate the internal Slack message presentation.
